parole.significato: V-shaped red trim on the front of an orderly’s jacket sleeve
parole.testo: Uncertain; either a modification of csúcs (“tip, peak”), or borrowed from Carpathian Ukrainian чічка (čička, “flower”).^((uk₁))^((uk₂))
From Ukrainian холошні (xološni, “winter peasant pants made of cloth”), from холоша (xološa, “leg of trousers”).

From Ukrainian коломийка (kolomyjka, “a Ukrainian folk dance”), named after Коломия (Kolomyja, “Kolomyia”), a town in Western Ukraine. (Probably unrelated to Belarusian каламажка (kalamažka) and Ukrainian каламайка (kalamajka).)
Borrowed from Ukrainian коза́к (kozák, “Cossack”), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *qazāq (“free man, adventurer”).

parole.significato: cold, bitter winter weather with drifting snow or sleet
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ukrainian зимонька́ (zymonʹká), diminutive of зима́ (zymá, “winter”).
